title: Byte-addressed lexical memory
summary: Attach a trainable raw-byte address table at final injection and inspect prepared UTF-8-derived addresses independently of a campaign.

steps.explanation: Prepared data supplies a causal raw-byte n-gram address for each token position; values are projected, gated, and added to the hidden residual.
observe: first byte lookup addresses in a full probe diagnostic

steps.explanation: Addresses come from the actual prompt and tokenizer's UTF-8 byte boundaries, not a second probe-only hash algorithm.
shapes: token suffix length and raw-byte length can differ

prerequisites: Prepare the selected tokenizer and byte-addressed data before training; a probe requires the configured tokenizer.
try_changes: Predict why a UTF-8 split token can differ from a token-ID suffix.
Change exactly one of table size, byte order, or injection placement.
Compare repeated byte and token addresses without treating either as semantic retrieval proof.
limits: Byte addresses are prepared-data features; the table is trainable lexical storage, not a semantic pack.
Repeated address diagnostics do not demonstrate semantic collisions, transfer, or task gains.

papers.title: Engram: A Neural Memory System for Language Models
papers.claim_boundary: The paper motivates memory questions; SparseLab's byte-addressed table is a local educational implementation, not a reproduction.
